quote: In relative terms, StoneDB's bulk-insert throughput was about 54 percent higher than KVLite's.
problem: Arithmetic error. A2 gives medians of 348 and 212; 348 / 212 is about 1.64, so StoneDB was about 64 percent higher, not 54.

quote: Marlin's higher write throughput comes from its batched write-ahead log, which groups concurrent writes into a single append.
problem: Causal mechanism stated as a finding. A1 says no profiler, tracing or ablation runs were collected for any store, so the mechanism rests only on the vendor README line in A7 (a design description). It is inference and should be labelled as such.

quote: Marlin's write advantage holds regardless of storage hardware or durability settings.
problem: Generalisation beyond the evidence. All runs were on one machine with one NVMe SSD and batched fsync (every 1,000 writes); per-write fsync was not tested (A1). Only in-sample results exist for this configuration.

quote: Marlin also serves random reads faster than StoneDB.
problem: Flat assertion on a small gap. The medians are 417 and 402 (A2), about 4 percent apart, and the five-run ranges overlap ([391-426] and [395-410]). The claim should be labelled as small and not clearly separated.

quote: Under the mixed workload, KVLite's median p99 latency was 4.2 ms, the worst of the three, against 3.1 ms for StoneDB and 2.9 ms for Marlin.
problem: Wrong figure. A3 gives KVLite's median p99 as 4.8 ms [4.5-5.2], not 4.2 ms. The ranking is unchanged, but the number is misquoted.

quote: StoneDB sustains its mixed-workload throughput over long-running operation.
problem: Claim beyond the evidence. The longest run was 6 minutes including warm-up, and A1 says no soak or multi-hour run was performed. A5 covers only five minutes, so long-running behaviour was not tested.

quote: As for what the projects say about themselves, Marlin's own documentation presents it as the right engine for write-intensive systems generally.
problem: Misquotes the source. The README line in A7 says Marlin is designed for write-intensive workloads whose reads mostly touch recently written keys. The body drops that qualifier and adds 'the right engine', which the README does not say.

quote: The appendix lists the software versions and configuration used, so that the run can be repeated.
problem: Overstated repeatability. A1 says the in-house harness is not yet published and no external reproduction has been done, so the appendix alone does not enable repetition. The body's own next-steps paragraph treats publication of the harness as a future plan.

quote: Wray kept a continuous day-by-day record of the winter.
problem: Contradicted by the appendix. E1 records no entries from 12 December 1741 to 26 January 1742 (46 days) and missing folios 31-34, and the body itself notes that several entries were written up later.

quote: The parish register shows 52 burials in 1742, which is 23 more than in 1741.
problem: Arithmetic error. E5(a) gives 33 burials for 1741; 52 minus 33 is 19, not 23.

quote: Of the 29 death entries in the journal, Wray names a fever as the cause in seven.
problem: Wrong count. E5(b) gives fever as the named cause in 5 entries (cold or frost in 6, no cause in 18).

quote: The frost alone accounts for the rise in burials in 1742.
problem: Causal claim the appendix does not support. Only 6 of 29 death entries name cold or frost, 18 name no cause, and nothing in the appendix tests other causes or links the journal to the register rise. At most this is an inference, and 'alone' is unsupported.

quote: Wray's burial entries have been checked against the parish register and found accurate.
problem: Overgeneralised verification. E6 Q8 shows the 1911 editor compared nine burial notices only and says the remainder were not checked. The body presents a partial check as a check of all entries and gives no source for it.

quote: Wray states that the vicar kept the tithe barn locked against the poor.
problem: Hearsay presented as Wray's assertion. Q5 (fol. 41r) reads 'It is said by some that our vicar, Mr. Hale, keeps the tithe barn locked' and 'I have not seen it with my own eyes'. Wray reports a rumour and disclaims it.

quote: The vestry responded by laying a rate for the poor, recorded on folio 38v.
problem: Inference presented as the journal's content. Q3 (fol. 38v) records a poor rate, but nothing in the appendix ties it to the mill or grain shortage, so 'responded' is an unlabelled causal link.

quote: The journal gives a representative picture of how rural parishes in the county fared that winter.
problem: Unsupported generalisation. E1 says the edition covers one parish and prints no records of other parishes or comparative material, so representativeness cannot be shown from this source.

quote: Of the 48 nurses who were screened but not randomized, most (31) declined to take part.
problem: Categories swapped. T2 gives 31 of the 48 as ineligible and 17 as declined.

quote: Across both arms, 56 of 64 participants (85.9%) completed the week 8 assessment.
problem: Arithmetic error. 56 of 64 is 87.5%, as T2 itself states; 85.9% is wrong.

quote: The reduction in insomnia severity persisted after the program ended.
problem: Untested claim. T1 says there is no assessment after week 8 and protocol 6.3 plans no follow-up, so persistence was never measured.

quote: The sleep-restriction module is what drove the improvement.
problem: Causal attribution the design cannot support. Protocol 3.1 says components are delivered only together and 'The study does not test individual components.' At most this is a hypothesis.

quote: Engagement with the program was high.
problem: Evaluative label without support. T5 shows a median of 5 of 8 modules, 2 participants completing none, and only 11 of 32 (34.4%) completing all eight. No benchmark is given for 'high'.

quote: These data show the program is safe for night-shift nurses.
problem: Overstated safety claim. Protocol 7.4 says the study is not powered to estimate adverse-event rates; there were 32 per arm at one site; and adverse events were collected differently by arm (weekly check-in in the app arm, week 8 in the control arm, per T1). Zero or two events cannot show safety.

quote: The findings apply to shift workers generally.
problem: Generalisation beyond the sample. The pilot enrolled registered nurses at one teaching hospital (T1); no other shift-worker group was studied.

quote: Below 3.0 kN the bracket has an effectively infinite fatigue life.
problem: Extrapolation stated as a result. F2 and F3 show no specimen was tested below 3.0 kN, so this is untested and should be labelled as an extrapolation at most.

quote: At 4.0 kN the bracket has a 75 percent chance of failing before two million cycles.
problem: In-sample proportion presented as a probability. It is 3 failures in 4 specimens, one flagged INTERRUPTED (F3), and F2 says no statistical analysis of the fatigue data was performed. It should be labelled as a descriptive count from n = 4.

quote: One of the four specimens reached the runout and the other three failed, the shortest at 1,138,000 cycles.
problem: Wrong figure. F3 gives F4-04 failing at 1,238,000 cycles, which is the shortest of the three failures; 1,138,000 appears nowhere in the table.

quote: The mean life at 5.0 kN was about 483,000 cycles.
problem: Arithmetic error. The F3 values 412,000, 366,000, 508,000 and 447,000 average 433,250 cycles, not about 483,000.

quote: The excess set in S08 is explained by its coming from a different material lot.
problem: Untested explanation stated as established. F4 and F5 show one specimen from lot B, a lot-B mill certificate not on file, and no sectioning, hardness or tensile tests scheduled. The lot link is a hypothesis.

quote: The bracket's performance carries over to the full range of service temperatures.
problem: Untested extrapolation. F2 says all tests ran at 20.1 to 22.6 C with no tests at other temperatures, while REQ-EN-003 (F1) requires operation from -30 C to +50 C.

quote: The fatigue programme was run in accordance with ASTM E466.
problem: Misstates the method. F1 quotes TP-221 as 'adapted from ASTM E466' and lists deviations in its section 4 (four specimens per level against a plan of six; load frame alignment not verified). The body omits both.

quote: The test plan and the laboratory log are reproduced in the appendix.
problem: Overstated. F1 quotes only extracts of the test plan, and F5 is labelled 'Laboratory log (extract)'. Neither is reproduced in full.
